root_motivation: Prod shows no distinguishable human signups after the one-URL fleet shipped (PRD-mcphost-funnel-truth, 10-06): the public surfaces today (mcphost.dev, the docs landed by PRD-mcphost-docs-one-url-flow) tell a reader to paste a URL into their client's own MCP settings, a path with at least three manual steps where other MCP servers offer one link. MCP clients already accept install links (Cursor's cursor://.../mcp/install deep link, VS Code's vscode:mcp/install deep link, Claude Code's `claude mcp add` command, Claude.ai's Add-custom-connector flow) -- this PRD renders those four forms from the running server's own hostname on a new /connect page, in the README, and in host_quickstart's response, so they never drift from the deployed endpoint, and counts clicks per client as funnel events with the origin label PRD-mcphost-funnel-truth already defined.
user_persona: A Cursor/VS Code/Claude Code/Claude.ai user who heard of mcphost and wants to try it in the client they already use, in one step, instead of hand-copying a URL into settings they have to go find; Operator Joe, whose digest (admin.funnel) gains an install_link_clicks line listing cursor/vscode/claude-code clicks by human visitors.

additional.personal_url_only_recoverable_from_path_: AC3 wants host_quickstart's install_links to carry the caller's personal /u/<secret>/mcp URL, but this host never stores a url secret in plaintext -- only its hash (db::find_tenant_by_url_secret_hash). The only call shape where the raw secret is available at all is a request that itself authenticated over /u/{secret}/mcp (handler::url_path_secret(parts) reads it straight off the live request's own URI). A header- or tenant_key-authenticated host.quickstart call therefore gets no install_links field at all -- additive, best-effort, same degrade shape control.rs's own plan_limits block already uses for a catalog-miss. This is exactly the PRD's own 'Tenant (any client)' user story: reconnecting through the personal URL and calling host.quickstart hands back the same four forms pre-filled, so a second machine connects pre-linked.
additional.oauth_funnel_events_reused_with_client_e: Technical considerations says 'reuses record_oauth_funnel_event's table or the activation funnel table (builder's choice)' and Migration/compatibility says 'no schema change beyond a new funnel event kind'. oauth_funnel_events (migration 0053) has no client column, so the client name rides inside the event string itself (install_link:cursor, install_link:vscode, ...) -- one more distinct event VALUE in an existing free-text column, not a new column or table, matching the PRD's own 'no schema change' line literally.
additional.the_digest_means_admin_funnel_and_health: This crate has two unrelated things both colloquially called 'funnel': the mcphost funnel CLI subcommand (src/funnel.rs, PRD-mcphost-tenant-attribution's real/synthetic split) and admin.funnel / /healthz's funnel_7d (the operator-facing report PRD-mcphost-funnel-truth's own AC4 test -- ftruth_ac04_digest_and_funnel_report_human_headline.rs -- explicitly calls 'the digest'). AC6's 'the digest' is read as the latter (the surface ftruth already extended with signups_human/by_origin), not the former, since that PRD's own test file names it that way and this PRD's own Technical considerations reuses the SAME funnel_origin vocabulary ftruth defined.
additional.connect_go_must_be_302_not_axum_redirect: AC5 pins '302 to the Cursor deep link' literally; axum::response::Redirect::to() is a 303 See Other by its own doc comment (Redirect::temporary/permanent are 307/308; there is no public 302 constructor), so connect_go builds the response manually via Response::builder().status(StatusCode::FOUND) -- the exact pattern src/vault.rs's own get_connect already uses for its dynamic-Location 302.
additional.four_forms_means_four_install_methods_no: Requirement 2's 'renders HTML with the four forms' and AC2's 'the page contains all four forms' read, in context of the Goals section ('Four install forms rendered from MCPHOST_PUBLIC_URL: Cursor deep link, VS Code deep link, Claude Code command, Claude.ai steps'), as four install METHODS -- not four literal <form> elements. /connect renders each as a plain <a href> (Cursor/VS Code, routed through /connect/go/<client> for AC5's click tracking) or <code>/<ol> text (Claude Code's command, Claude.ai's steps), all of it plain markup with zero JavaScript.
additional.claude_ai_steps_wording_avoids_a_literal: The first Claude.ai step originally read 'Open Settings -> Connectors -> Add custom connector.'; render_connect_page HTML-escapes every interpolated string (claim::html_escape), which would turn that literal '>' into '>' in the rendered page -- silently breaking the no-JS page's own readability and any test comparing against the raw string. Reworded to 'Open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector.' (no HTML-significant characters at all) rather than special-casing escaping for this one string.

five_whys_trace.q: Why would rendering install links actually move the needle, when the mechanism behind them (implicit signup on bare /mcp) is already built and live?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own Failure-under-this-seed line says so directly: this is a missing arrival SURFACE, not a broken mechanism -- the one-URL flow already turns a first call into a tenant, but a visitor who doesn't know their client's own MCP settings path never gets there. Three manual steps (find settings, find the URL, paste it correctly) is enough friction that most visitors who 'heard of mcphost' never try it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why four separate forms instead of one generic 'paste this URL' instruction everywhere?
five_whys_trace.a: Each client's own install mechanism is different and already documented by that client (Cursor/VS Code's own URI-scheme deep links skip the settings-navigation step entirely; Claude Code has no deep link, only a CLI command; Claude.ai has neither, only a UI flow) -- rendering each client's own preferred mechanism is strictly fewer steps than making every client follow the lowest-common-denominator 'paste a URL' path.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build one install_links module instead of writing the Cursor/VS Code/Claude Code strings directly into /connect, host_quickstart, and the README separately?
five_whys_trace.a: Technical considerations says it directly: 'deep-link formats change; keep them in one module with fixtures and a comment per client naming the doc page and the date checked' -- three hand-copies of the same format drift independently the moment one client changes its deep-link shape, the exact failure mode this module's own doc comment and clink_ac01's fixtures exist to catch.

five_whys_trace.q: Why click-tracking (AC5/AC6) at all, if the goal is just 'make it easier to connect'?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own success metrics table has no way to measure 'did this surface work' without it -- 'human install-link clicks per week' is a named target metric (>= 5, two weeks after deploy), and without per-client click events there is no signal distinguishing 'nobody found /connect' from 'people found it but didn't click through', which is exactly the gap PRD-mcphost-funnel-truth's own grounding (no distinguishable human signups after the one-URL fleet shipped) is trying to close.

five_whys_trace.q: Why humans-only in the digest (AC6), rather than every click regardless of origin?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD-mcphost-funnel-truth already established that fleet/probe traffic (deploy smoke tests, wm-build live verifiers) hits this host's own routes regardless of any real visitor, and a digest that can't tell a human's click from a deploy probe's is exactly the conflated-number problem that PRD existed to fix -- this PRD's own Requirements line says 'funnel events reuse ... with origin set per funnel-truth' specifically so AC6 doesn't reintroduce that same conflation one surface later.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Can host_quickstart's install_links show a REAL personal /u/<secret>/mcp URL for every authenticated call, or only some?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Only when the call itself authenticated over /u/{secret}/mcp -- see hard_constraints.personal_url_only_recoverable_from_path_secret_auth. A header-/tenant_key-authenticated call gets no install_links field; this is additive and best-effort, not a regression, since no prior response had this field either.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the install_link funnel event need a new table/column for the client name, given oauth_funnel_events has none?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- the client name rides inside the event string itself (install_link:cursor, etc.), one more value in an existing free-text column; see hard_constraints.oauth_funnel_events_reused_with_client_encoded_in_event_not_a_new_column.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does AC5's '302' tolerate axum::response::Redirect::to's default 303?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- read literally; axum's Redirect::to is documented as 303 See Other, so connect_go builds the 302 response manually. See hard_constraints.connect_go_must_be_302_not_axum_redirects_default_303.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which existing surface does AC6's 'the digest' refer to -- the mcphost funnel CLI, or admin.funnel/healthz's funnel_7d?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: admin.funnel/healthz's funnel_7d -- the surface PRD-mcphost-funnel-truth's own AC4 test explicitly calls 'the digest'. See hard_constraints.the_digest_means_admin_funnel_and_healthz_funnel_7d_not_a_new_mcphost_funnel_cli_line.
